description: The pie chart visually represents the proportional distribution of six emotion categories within the IEMOCAP dataset, based on the number of utterances per category, with each slice labeled externally and its percentage value displayed inside. The largest segment is “Frustration,” colored light blue, accounting for 25.1% of the total. Adjacent to it is “Neutral,” in dark blue, at 23.1%. Following clockwise, “Happiness” appears in red at 8.1%, then “Excitement” in pink at 14.1%, “Sadness” in orange at 14.7%, and “Anger” in yellow at 14.9%. Notably, the caption’s stated percentages for Anger (15.9%) and Happiness (10.1%) do not match the values shown in the chart (14.9% and 8.1%, respectively), indicating a discrepancy between the visual data and the accompanying text. The chart does not visually emphasize any slice through explosion or shading, and the segments are arranged in a roughly descending order clockwise from Frustration, though not strictly sorted. The overall layout prioritizes clarity, with distinct colors and external labels aiding interpretation.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset, with percentages displayed relative to the number of utterances. Frustration is the largest category, accounting for approximately 25.1% of the data, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. Anger and Sadness are nearly equal, with Anger slightly higher at 15.9% and Sadness at 14.7%. Excitement and Happiness are the smallest categories, with Happiness at 10.1% and Excitement at 14.1%. Notably, the data suggests a consistent decline in positive emotions (Excitement and Happiness) compared to negative ones (Frustration, Anger, and Sadness). The chart provides a clear visual representation of the emotional distribution, with labels positioned outside each slice for clarity.
